Title: Aurora Ransomware Group Utilizes AI Tools for Network Intrusions

Victim.Description: Over 20 organizations across nine countries targeted by Aurora ransomware.
Victim.Geography: United States, Germany, Netherlands, Canada, United Kingdom

diamond_model_summary: The Aurora ransomware group, a Russian-speaking cybercrime entity, has been observed using AI tools like Cursor and Gryxa to infiltrate networks and deploy ransomware. Their operations targeted over 20 organizations across nine countries, employing advanced techniques such as NTLM relay attacks and lateral movement via SMB, LDAP, WinRM, RDP, and RPC. The group's motivation is financial gain, achieved through ransom payments and cryptocurrency laundering. Their infrastructure includes exposed directories and cryptocurrency wallets, while their capabilities are enhanced by AI-assisted planning and execution.
doc_summary: Aurora ransomware group, also known as Aur0ra, has been observed using SpaceX's AI-powered coding assistant Cursor to infiltrate networks. The group, associated with Russian-speaking cybercriminals, targeted over 20 organizations across nine countries between April and July 2026. The attack chain involved aggressive email bombing, phone calls posing as IT help desk personnel, and lateral movement via SMB, LDAP, WinRM, RDP, and RPC. The group used Cursor for planning attacks in Russian, excluding CIS ranges. The ransomware, written in Zig, has both Windows and Linux versions. The Windows variant deletes volume shadow copies and disables System Restore, while the Linux variant kills virtual machines before encryption. The group also used NTLM relay attacks and certificate attacks with Certipy. The Gryxa toolkit, another AI-assisted tool, was used for initial access operations targeting 324 hosts, leveraging legitimate RMM software for covert access and credential theft.
kill_chain_summary: Aurora ransomware group's attack chain begins with reconnaissance using AI tools to plan attacks, followed by weaponization through the development of ransomware in Zig. Delivery is achieved via email phishing and phone calls, leading to exploitation of vulnerabilities for initial access. Installation involves deploying ransomware on compromised systems, while command and control is established through application layer protocols. Actions on objectives include data exfiltration and ransomware deployment, with the group leveraging NTLM relay attacks and certificate attacks to achieve their goals.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for the Aurora ransomware incident includes various indicators of compromise. Hash values of the ransomware binaries, IP addresses used for command and control, and domain names associated with the group's infrastructure are critical for detection. Network host artifacts, such as scheduled tasks and startup items, provide additional detection opportunities. Tools like Cursor and Gryxa, along with TTPs such as NTLM relay attacks and lateral movement techniques, are essential for understanding the group's operations and developing effective countermeasures.

doc_summary: The Manchester Airports Group (MAG), the United Kingdom's largest airport operator, experienced a data breach claimed by the extortion group FulcrumSec. The breach affected Manchester, London Stansted, and East Midlands airports, with data from car park, lounge, and Fast Track bookings, as well as in-airport Wi-Fi registrations. FulcrumSec accessed the data using exposed Iterable API credentials in client-side JavaScript. The group plans to publish the stolen data but may redact sensitive information to prevent real-world harm. MAG confirmed that affected customers were contacted and advised to remain vigilant against phishing attempts. The breach did not compromise passenger safety or aviation security.

doc_summary: Microsoft has disclosed a new ClickFix variant, TerminalFix, targeting organizations across multiple sectors. The campaign uses compromised websites to serve fake Cloudflare CAPTCHA verifications, prompting users to execute malicious PowerShell commands. The attack chain involves DLL sideloading, steganographic payload extraction, Active Directory reconnaissance, and a custom reverse-tunnel implant for persistent network-level proxy access. The PowerShell command downloads a ZIP archive with a legitimate binary and a rogue DLL to initiate the attack. The sideloaded DLL retrieves payloads from external domains, establishes persistence, and deploys a Python-based reverse-tunnel C2 implant. The backdoor tunnels TCP traffic to attacker-controlled infrastructure. Microsoft warns of potential privilege escalation, security control disarmament, data exfiltration, and ransomware deployment. Mitigation includes restricting PowerShell execution, monitoring for DLL sideloading, and enabling script block logging.
kill_chain_summary: The TerminalFix attack chain begins with reconnaissance through Active Directory, followed by weaponization using steganography to hide payloads. Delivery occurs via compromised websites serving fake CAPTCHA verifications. Exploitation involves tricking users into executing PowerShell commands. Installation is achieved through DLL sideloading, leading to command and control via a reverse-tunnel implant. The attacker can then perform actions on objectives, such as privilege escalation and data exfiltration.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for the TerminalFix campaign includes domain names and network host artifacts as key indicators. Title: Critical Vulnerabilities in WordPress Plugins and Themes

Victim.Description: Users of affected WordPress plugins and themes

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves critical vulnerabilities in WordPress plugins and themes, potentially leading to authentication bypass, account takeover, and arbitrary code execution. The adversary exploits a PHP object injection vulnerability (CVE-2026-82222) in the GiveWP plugin, leveraging a broken 'safe unserialize' helper and a gadget chain. The infrastructure and specific adversary details remain unidentified, but the victims are users of the affected WordPress plugins and themes.
doc_summary: Multiple critical security flaws have been disclosed in WordPress plugins and themes, including WPMU DEV Dashboard, Avada, TranslatePress, Pods, and GiveWP, that could lead to authentication bypass, account takeover, and arbitrary code execution. The vulnerabilities, according to Wordfence and Patchstack, are listed below. The flaw chains a broken 'safe unserialize' helper, a donation flow that feeds that helper attacker-controlled data, and a gadget chain in code that GiveWP ships, Patchstack said about CVE-2026-82222. This case shows how PHP object injection turns into remote code execution when three ingredients line up: a place to store an attacker-controlled serialized object, code that later unserializes it, and a gadget chain in loaded classes. The root causes are common: trusting a serialization sanitizer that does not actually strip objects, unserializing data read back from the database as if it were trusted, and shipping development-only libraries into production where they provide ready-made gadget chains.

doc_summary: Brave browser version 1.94 introduces a new feature called 'Email Aliases' to enhance user privacy by allowing the creation of disposable email addresses. This feature aims to protect users from phishing attacks and data breaches by keeping real email addresses hidden. Brave uses data isolation to prevent identity inference through cookies and caches, but email addresses stored on servers pose a privacy risk. The new feature blocks cross-site identity matching and reduces spam. Users must create a free Brave Account to use email aliases, which are authenticated using OPAQUE, a password-authenticated key exchange standardized as RFC 9807. This reduces exposure to password logging and memory-scraping attacks. The system is free for up to five aliases, with a paid Premium version planned. Messages are forwarded in an encrypted state and deleted from servers after delivery. Brave warns that forwarded messages may initially land in spam folders.

doc_summary: VulnCheck disclosed two undocumented factory implants, SPEAKINGSTONE and DARKLANTERN, in firmware for routers by Shenzhen Zhibotong Electronics (ZBT). The vulnerabilities affect models like ZBT-WE826-T2, with firmware built in 2019. VulnCheck published IoCs and recommended blocking specific ports. The implants were found in routers sold by ZBT and resellers, with significant impact on China Mobile's network.

doc_summary: Cybersecurity researchers have identified a series of cyber campaigns targeting government and diplomatic organizations in Romania, Spain, and Türkiye from September 2025 to April 2026. These campaigns, attributed to the Russian state-sponsored group APT28, also known as Fancy Bear or BlueDelta, involved the deployment of a new backdoor named HOOKEDGE. This malware is distributed via macro-enabled Microsoft Word documents with diplomatic-themed lures. The campaigns show significant overlap with previous APT28 operations using the HEADLACE backdoor. HOOKEDGE uses webhook[.]site services for command-and-control, payload staging, and data exfiltration. The malware's delivery mechanism involves writing files to the %userprofile% directory and creating scheduled tasks for persistence. BlueDelta has refined its tactics to evade detection and adapt to infrastructure constraints, such as webhook[.]site's API limits. The campaigns highlight the need for organizations to block macro execution from internet-originated documents and monitor for scheduled task abuse and unusual network connections.
kill_chain_summary: APT28's campaign follows a structured kill chain: reconnaissance to identify targets, weaponization of macro-enabled documents, delivery via email, exploitation through macro execution, installation of HOOKEDGE via scheduled tasks, command and control using webhook[.]site, and actions on objectives including data exfiltration. The campaign demonstrates advanced persistence and evasion tactics.

The installer triggers a DLL side-loading chain using a signed Tencent executable, delivering interim payloads that deploy the vulnerable driver and launch the Spark RAT. The attack involves multi-stage payload delivery, persistence through Windows services, and Microsoft Defender exclusions.

The attack was reported to NVIDIA and other major tech companies, with a public release of the attack code scheduled for November 2026.

doc_summary: Meta has reached a proposed settlement worth up to $18 billion with a coalition of 52 attorneys general over allegations that Facebook and Instagram were designed to encourage compulsive use by children and teenagers. The lawsuit, filed in 2023 by California Attorney General Rob Bonta, accused Meta of misleading users about the risks of its platforms and illegally collecting data from children under 13, violating COPPA and California laws. Under the agreement, Meta will introduce new restrictions for users under 18, including a default two-hour daily usage limit, nighttime restrictions, and enhanced parental supervision tools. An independent auditor will oversee compliance, and Meta will be prohibited from making false claims about safety features. The agreement includes $18 billion in payments over ten years, with $12.7 billion going to participating states and $5.3 billion contingent on YouTube and TikTok adopting similar changes. California is expected to receive between $1.5 billion and $2.1 billion, earmarked for mental health and social media harm prevention. Meta anticipates $10 billion in legal expenses by the third quarter of 2026. The agreement also establishes a research foundation focused on teen well-being and social media use.

doc_summary: Cybersecurity researchers have identified new infrastructure and malware linked to Nimbus Manticore, an Iranian state-sponsored hacking group associated with the IRGC. Group-IB's analysis highlights the group's activity in 2026, linking it to Tortoiseshell and the Charming Kitten cluster. Tortoiseshell has been active since 2018, targeting defense, aerospace, IT, and military sectors in the Middle East and the United States. The group has used job opportunity-themed social engineering attacks to deliver malware. Group-IB discovered Tortoiseshell infrastructure in Europe and the Middle East, an SSH-based tunneling utility, and a C++ backdoor similar to TWOSTROKE. Kaspersky reported the use of a new Windows backdoor, NightLedger, and custom WebSocket tunnelers, BridgeHead and ArcBridge, for persistent access in attacks across the Middle East, Africa, and South Asia. A reverse SSH tunneling tool masquerades as the Windows Terminal Server SDK API, connecting to infrastructure at 172.86.98.113 on port 443. The TWOSTROKE backdoor collects system information, loads DLLs, manipulates files, and maintains persistence, using hard-coded C2 servers for HTTPS connections.

doc_summary: Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed details of a new adversary-in-the-middle (AitM) phishing toolkit called NovaCookies that targets Microsoft 365 sign-ins. The toolkit is a subscription-based phishing platform costing $320/month, used to capture authenticated sessions. It has targeted hundreds of organizations across sectors in the United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Germany, Israel, and United Arab Emirates. NovaCookies uses genuine Docusign envelopes to lure victims, routing them through legitimate sign-in endpoints before reaching attacker-controlled infrastructure. The toolkit is advertised via Telegram and assessed to be a variant of the Sneaky 2FA phishing kit. Unlike Sneaky 2FA, NovaCookies includes flows for other identity providers like Okta and Entra domains federated to GoDaddy. The phishing URLs often use alternating-case labels to appear legitimate. The attack employs OAuth error-redirect techniques and anti-analysis checks to evade security scanners. The disclosure highlights the growing trend of phishing-as-a-service (PhaaS) in the cybercrime underground.
kill_chain_summary: The NovaCookies attack follows a structured kill chain, beginning with the delivery of phishing emails using Docusign notifications as decoys. Exploitation occurs through OAuth error-redirect techniques to capture credentials. The attack culminates in the capture of authenticated sessions and credentials, with the adversary leveraging a phishing-as-a-service model to facilitate these actions. Defensive evasion tactics include anti-analysis checks and Cloudflare gates.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for the NovaCookies incident includes domain names like fordmotbvmorcompany.vu and tools such as NovaCookies and Sneaky 2FA. Title: Unpatched Vulnerabilities in Kaltura's HTML5 Video Player Library

Victim.Description: Kaltura's customers and shared CDN infrastructure.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves two unpatched vulnerabilities in Kaltura's HTML5 video player library, allowing remote attackers to read arbitrary files and execute code. The vulnerabilities stem from unsafe deserialization in the mwEmbedLoader.php endpoint. The affected infrastructure includes Kaltura's shared CDN and customer installations. No specific adversary or campaign is identified, but the potential impact is high due to the exposure of sensitive data and code execution capabilities.
doc_summary: The CERT Coordination Center disclosed two unpatched vulnerabilities in Kaltura's HTML5 video player library, tracked as CVE-2026-19913 and CVE-2026-19912. These vulnerabilities allow remote, unauthenticated attackers to read arbitrary files and execute code on a server. Both flaws stem from unsafe deserialization in the mwEmbedLoader.php endpoint of the mwEmbed player library, distributed as html5lib. No authentication or Kaltura session token is required, and network access to the endpoint is the only precondition. CERT/CC was unable to reach Kaltura to coordinate these vulnerabilities. Administrators are advised to restrict or disable external access to the endpoint and enforce a strict allow-list for the ServiceUrl parameter. No exploitation had been reported at the time of writing, and neither CVE appeared in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog as of August 25, 2026. The vulnerabilities affect customer installations and Kaltura's shared CDN infrastructure. The file read issue, CVE-2026-19913, involves the ServiceUrl parameter, which mwEmbedLoader.php accepts and uses as the target URL for backend API requests. The KalturaClientBase PHP client fetches the URL and passes it to PHP's unserialize() without validation. CVE-2026-19912 allows code execution via the uiconf_id request parameter, which is appended to the cache folder path without sanitization. The vulnerabilities affect html5lib v2.45, v2.103, and earlier releases.
kill_chain_summary: The vulnerabilities in Kaltura's HTML5 video player library represent a significant risk, allowing remote attackers to exploit unsafe deserialization for arbitrary file read and code execution. The exploitation stage is critical, as it involves exploiting public-facing applications without requiring authentication. The lack of a patch increases the urgency for remediation measures, such as restricting access to the vulnerable endpoint and enforcing strict allow-lists. The incident highlights the importance of securing deserialization processes and maintaining communication with vendors for timely vulnerability management.

doc_summary: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) conducted simultaneous red team assessments on two critical infrastructure organizations, revealing stark differences in defensive outcomes. Organization A, part of the Government Services and Facilities Sector, was fully compromised due to default credentials, misconfigured Active Directory Certificate Services, and poor SOC coordination. In contrast, Organization B, in the Water and Wastewater Systems Sector, quickly detected and isolated the attack, preventing further intrusion. The advisory, AA26-237A, highlights the importance of effective SOC processes and personnel in cybersecurity defense. Key vulnerabilities included cleartext credentials, static AWS keys, and misconfigured SCCM files. The report underscores the role of people and processes over tools in cybersecurity effectiveness.

Title: Analysis of SLEEPWALKER Backdoor Targeting ESET Management Agent

Victim.Description: No specific victims identified; potential targets include systems running ESET Management Agent.

diamond_model_summary: The SLEEPWALKER backdoor represents a sophisticated adversary operation targeting systems running ESET Management Agent. The adversary employs advanced techniques such as DLL side-loading and a custom instruction set for command execution. The infrastructure relies on compromised host network interfaces and VMware's VMCI for communication. No specific victims have been identified, but the operation is consistent with a targeted, well-resourced attack.
doc_summary: An independent malware researcher documented a Windows backdoor named SLEEPWALKER, which remains inactive in memory until triggered by a specific network packet. The backdoor is a 64-bit DLL designed to be side-loaded into ESET Management Agent's ERAAgent.exe, impersonating Microsoft's dpapi.dll. It uses AES-256-CCM encryption and a unique 23-instruction language for command execution. The malware does not contain built-in domains or IPs, making detection challenging. It relies on side-loading for persistence and requires local admin rights for installation. The backdoor's communication includes TCP, UDP, ICMP, SMB named pipes, raw capture, and VMware's VMCI. No public attribution or victim identification has been made, and ESET has not issued an advisory as of August 26.
kill_chain_summary: The SLEEPWALKER backdoor follows a complex kill chain involving weaponization through the development of a custom backdoor, installation via DLL side-loading, and command and control through specific network packet triggers. The backdoor's actions on objectives include executing commands in memory using a unique instruction set. Detection and remediation efforts focus on monitoring unauthorized DLLs, network traffic, and employing YARA rules.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for the SLEEPWALKER backdoor includes several challenging indicators such as the unique instruction set and side-loading technique. The absence of built-in domains or IPs makes detection difficult, emphasizing the need for behavioral analysis and monitoring of network traffic. The use of AES-256-CCM encryption and VMCI communication further complicates detection efforts.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves an unknown threat actor exploiting a critical vulnerability in Gitea (CVE-2026-60004) to deploy a cryptocurrency miner. The adversary leverages Gitea's open registration to gain repository write access and execute arbitrary commands. The capability includes exploiting the diffpatch endpoint for remote code execution. The infrastructure involves Gitea instances with open registration, and the victim is primarily technology sector entities using vulnerable Gitea versions. The attack's objective is financial gain through cryptojacking.
doc_summary: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) issued a warning about active exploitation of a critical vulnerability, CVE-2026-60004, in Gitea. This flaw allows remote code execution via the diffpatch endpoint, enabling attackers to execute arbitrary shell commands. Security researcher Shai Rod discovered the issue, affecting Gitea versions from 1.17 to 1.27.1. An analysis by developer Andrey revealed a cryptojacking campaign exploiting this vulnerability, deploying a cryptocurrency miner on a Gitea instance. The attack leveraged Gitea's default open registration, allowing unauthenticated users to gain repository write access. The incident was detected after a hosting provider reported excessive CPU usage. CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, urging federal agencies to patch by August 28, 2026.
kill_chain_summary: The attack begins with reconnaissance to identify Gitea instances with open registration. The adversary weaponizes a payload to exploit CVE-2026-60004, delivering it via the diffpatch endpoint. Exploitation occurs as the attacker gains initial access and executes arbitrary commands. Installation involves deploying a cryptocurrency miner, establishing command and control through HTTPS. The final stage, actions on objectives, sees the miner utilizing system resources for cryptojacking. Detection and remediation focus on monitoring registration activity, patching Gitea, and securing configurations.

Title: Malicious Use of npm Mirrors for Phishing via Fake Cloudflare CAPTCHA

Victim.Description: Users redirected to phishing sites via npm-hosted HTML.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves threat actors using npm and its mirrors to host malicious HTML pages that impersonate Cloudflare CAPTCHAs. The adversary's capability includes using npm as storage for phishing pages, leveraging JavaScript obfuscation for redirection. The infrastructure involves npm mirrors like UNPKG and npmmirror, with victims being users redirected to phishing sites.
doc_summary: Threat actors are exploiting npm and its mirrors to host malicious HTML pages that mimic Cloudflare CAPTCHAs, redirecting users to attacker-controlled sites. This technique, first identified in July, involves npm packages like 'china_airlines' using fake verification pages. OX Security found 24 such packages. Unlike typical npm threats, these packages don't infect developers' systems but use npm as storage for phishing pages. Platforms like UNPKG and npmmirror allow direct access to these HTML files, turning them into free hosting for phishing. The HTML impersonates Cloudflare's CAPTCHA, executing obfuscated JavaScript to redirect users. Initial redirects led to microcloud.homes and login.microsofte.live, with some resolving to Microsoft's Outlook login. Newer methods use api.keyval.org to dynamically change redirect URLs. OX warns that npm packages may persist on mirrors even after removal from the registry. The incident highlights the use of legitimate infrastructure for malicious purposes.
kill_chain_summary: The attack begins with the weaponization of malicious HTML pages mimicking Cloudflare CAPTCHA, hosted on npm mirrors. Victim.Description: NVIDIA NemoClaw users, particularly those using Ollama instances on non-loopback interfaces.
Victim.Security_Posture: Vulnerable due to improper binding and lack of header validation.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves an adversary exploiting a vulnerability in NVIDIA NemoClaw to gain unauthorized control over the Ollama instance. The adversary uses DNS rebinding and API manipulation to modify chat templates, allowing persistent control over AI model behavior. The attack infrastructure includes a webpage controlled by the attacker and DNS manipulation. Victims are NVIDIA NemoClaw users, particularly those using Ollama instances on non-loopback interfaces. The impact severity is high, with potential risks to AI model configurations and chat templates.
doc_summary: Oasis Security disclosed a vulnerability in NVIDIA NemoClaw that allows an attacker-controlled webpage to take unauthenticated control of the local Ollama instance. The issue affects NVIDIA's open-source reference stack for running agents like OpenClaw inside OpenShell sandboxes. The vulnerability involves binding the model server to every network interface, allowing API access to modify the model's chat template. This can lead to hidden instructions being applied to every conversation. The attack chain includes DNS rebinding, which resolves the attacker's domain to their server and then to 127.0.0.1, bypassing CORS protections. The vulnerability was reported to NVIDIA's PSIRT, and a fix was implemented in NemoClaw v0.0.35 for macOS and Linux, but not for Windows and WSL. The issue was tested on macOS with Firefox, and the full chain was documented. Ollama introduced validation in response to a previous disclosure, but skips it when bound to a non-loopback address. The report highlights the need for verifying Host and Origin headers to prevent such attacks.

doc_summary: Bad actors are exploiting severe unauthenticated authentication bypasses in the Xecurify miniOrange SAML 2.0 Single Sign On plugin, allowing attackers to sign in as any WordPress user, including administrators. The vulnerabilities, disclosed by Patchstack, involve the mo_saml_validate_signature() function's loose boolean check on the openssl_verify() return value, leading to CVE-2026-15981. This flaw enables attackers to log in as any WordPress user by submitting a crafted SAMLResponse with a malformed signature, bypassing verification and calling wp_set_auth_cookie() for the targeted account. DigitalOcean discovered these vulnerabilities after observing an anomalous WordPress admin session attempt. The scanning activity is linked to opportunistic scanning from multiple IP addresses. WordPress site owners are advised to apply the latest fixes due to the availability of proof-of-concept code that chains the flaws to obtain admin privileges.

CERT/CC coordinated a public disclosure, and BleepingComputer has contacted Calix for comments.

doc_summary: Cybersecurity researchers have identified a campaign distributing the Weedhack malware family by masquerading as Minecraft clients. McAfee Labs detected over 6,300 attempts to access malicious sites, which mimic legitimate gaming websites. The campaign uses SEO poisoning and YouTube to redirect traffic to fake domains, deploying JAR payloads that collect system information and steal sensitive data. Nearly half of the malicious URLs were Discord links, with others hosted on MediaFire and GitHub. The campaign also uses AI-powered website builders to create convincing malicious sites. The legitimate client is hosted on GitHub and Modrinth, but attackers have spoofed websites to outrank official sources. The malware is spread via Discord, Reddit, and other channels, with JAR files hosted on Planet Minecart and EndMods. Users are advised to keep devices updated, use trusted sources, and scan files before opening.

Title: Critical Security Flaw in Keycloak Allows Account Takeover

Victim.Description: Users of Keycloak identity and access management server

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves a critical vulnerability in Keycloak, allowing unauthenticated attackers to reset passwords and take over accounts. The flaw is due to improper state validation in the reset-credentials flow. Red Hat has released patches and advisories to mitigate the risk. The vulnerability is rated 9.1 on the CVSS scale, indicating a high potential impact on affected systems.
doc_summary: Red Hat and the Keycloak project released patches for a critical security flaw in Keycloak, an open-source identity and access management server. The vulnerability, CVE-2026-18963, allows unauthenticated remote attackers to take over user accounts by exploiting a weak password recovery mechanism. Rated 9.1 on the CVSS scale, the flaw involves improper state validation in the reset-credentials authentication flow. Users are advised to update to Keycloak version 26.7.2 or apply updates for Red Hat builds 26.4.15 and 26.6.6. No evidence of exploitation exists as of August 24, 2026. Red Hat issued errata RHSA-2026:56519, RHSA-2026:56520, RHSA-2026:56523, and RHSA-2026:56524. Temporary mitigation involves disabling the 'Forgot password' feature. The flaw was reported by James Paremain.
kill_chain_summary: The attack chain involves exploiting a vulnerability in Keycloak's password reset mechanism, allowing attackers to bypass authentication and reset user passwords. This leads to unauthorized access and potential account takeover. The exploitation stage is critical, with Red Hat providing patches and mitigation strategies to address the flaw. Monitoring and disabling the 'Forgot password' feature are recommended.

doc_summary: A critical vulnerability identified as CVE-2026-32475 was discovered in the Elementor Pro WordPress plugin, affecting versions before 4.2.2. This flaw allows attackers to upload executable files for remote code execution on the server. The vulnerability stems from the File Upload module, which mishandles empty filename uploads due to separate loops for file validation and processing. An attacker can exploit this by crafting a multipart upload with an empty filename followed by a malicious PHP payload. The validation routine exits after the first part, while the processing step moves the PHP file to a public directory, enabling arbitrary code execution. Patchstack learned of the vulnerability on July 16, and a fix was prepared by the plugin developer the next day. Administrators are advised to update to the latest version and check for rogue files in the 'wp-content/uploads/elementor/forms/' directory.

doc_summary: The U.S. government has issued a warning about an active threat targeting critical infrastructure organizations using AI-generated exploit scripts. The threat actors are focusing on Siemens S7 Series Programmable Logic Controllers (PLCs) to conduct reconnaissance and capability development. The activity is broader than Siemens PLCs and involves internet scanning services like Censys and ZoomEye to identify vulnerable PLCs. The targeted sectors include Critical Manufacturing, Energy, Water and Wastewater Systems, Chemical, Food and Agriculture, and Commercial Facilities. The exploitation of poorly secured PLCs could lead to industrial process disruptions, safety incidents, and data compromise. The threat actors use AI to generate scripts for initial access, credential access, and denial of service. A custom Python script with open-source libraries like snap7.dll is used to mimic legitimate monitoring utilities. The agencies recommend updating PLCs, isolating them from the internet, and employing strong access controls.
kill_chain_summary: The kill chain stages identified in this incident include reconnaissance, where threat actors use internet scanning services to identify vulnerable PLCs. pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes tools such as custom Python scripts and open-source libraries like snap7.dll. doc_summary: The Mabna Institute, an Iran-based company, has been charged by the U.S. Department of Justice for conducting cyber intrusions into computer systems of 144 U.S.-based universities, 178 foreign universities, and various private sector companies and government agencies. The stolen data was sold through websites Megapaper.ir and Gigapaper.ir. The U.S. Department of State is offering a $10 million reward for information about five of the defendants. The Mabna Institute represents the privatization of state espionage, with the IRGC as an anchor client.

Title: CDN Tsunami: HTTP/3 to HTTP/1.1 Amplification Attacks on Major CDNs

Victim.Description: Websites hosted on vulnerable CDNs

diamond_model_summary: The CDN Tsunami attack demonstrates a sophisticated exploitation of HTTP/3 to HTTP/1.1 conversion vulnerabilities in major CDNs. The adversary, likely researchers, aimed to highlight these vulnerabilities. The capability involves leveraging QPACK dynamic table for amplification. The infrastructure includes CDNs like Alibaba, Baidu, and Tencent. Victims are websites hosted on these CDNs, facing high impact severity due to amplified traffic.
doc_summary: Cybersecurity researchers disclosed two denial-of-service attacks named CDN Tsunami, targeting major CDNs like Alibaba, Baidu, Cloudflare, Amazon CloudFront, Fastly, and Tencent. These attacks exploit the conversion of HTTP/3 traffic to HTTP/1.1, amplifying requests up to 350x against origin servers. The attacks, HTTP/3 Bandwidth Amplification (HBA) and HTTP/3 Connection Amplification (HCA), leverage QPACK dynamic table vulnerabilities. Alibaba, Baidu, and Tencent are most affected, with mitigations applied at the CDN level. No CVEs assigned, and no wild exploitation reported. The research is credited to universities in Singapore, Fuzhou, Sheffield, and Johns Hopkins, and will be presented at a symposium in Rome in 2026.
kill_chain_summary: The CDN Tsunami attack follows a structured kill chain, starting with reconnaissance to identify vulnerable CDNs supporting HTTP/3. Weaponization involves crafting HTTP/3 requests to exploit the conversion process. Delivery is achieved by sending these requests to the CDN. Exploitation occurs through amplification of traffic, overwhelming origin servers. Command and control is maintained by keeping connections open. The final objective is to cause denial-of-service through traffic amplification.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The CDN Tsunami attack primarily involves TTPs related to HTTP/3 and QPACK exploitation, making it challenging to detect and mitigate. No specific hash values, IP addresses, or domain names are identified, focusing on protocol-level vulnerabilities. The attack leverages CDN infrastructure, highlighting the need for robust detection and mitigation strategies at the CDN level. The pyramid of pain emphasizes the difficulty in addressing such protocol-based attacks.

Title: Zombie Card Attack on Expired Visa Contactless Cards

Victim.Description: The victims are potentially users of Visa contactless cards with expired cards that have not been properly deactivated.
Victim.Security_Posture: Vulnerable due to lack of expiration date verification

diamond_model_summary: The 'Zombie Card' attack demonstrates a vulnerability in Visa contactless credit cards where expired cards can be revived for transactions by manipulating the expiration date read by POS terminals over NFC. The attack requires physical possession of the card or sustained NFC proximity, and a MitM relay setup. The research highlights the need for improved expiration date verification by issuers.
doc_summary: Researchers at the University of Massachusetts Amherst demonstrated an attack named 'Zombie Card' that revives expired Visa contactless credit cards for in-store purchases by rewriting the expiration date read by a POS terminal over NFC. The attack requires physical possession of the expired card or sustained NFC proximity, plus a MitM relay between the card and terminal. The account must remain open under the same PAN, and the issuing bank must not re-check the expiry during authorization. The attack was tested against five major US banks, with varying results. The research was presented at the 35th USENIX Security Symposium in 2026. Visa and affected banks were notified in 2025, but no CVE has been assigned, and no exploitation has been reported. The attack exploits Visa's Kernel 3, which does not require consistent binding of expiration dates, allowing the relay to rewrite the terminal-facing date. The attack was tested using NFC-capable Android phones running custom software. No EMV's optional Relay Resistance Protocol was implemented in the testbed.
kill_chain_summary: The attack involves exploiting Visa Kernel 3's handling of expiration dates, allowing attackers to manipulate the expiration date read by POS terminals. The attack requires physical possession of the card or sustained NFC proximity, and a MitM relay setup. The objective is to complete transactions using expired cards, highlighting the need for improved expiration date verification by issuers.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The 'Zombie Card' attack leverages a vulnerability in Visa contactless credit cards, specifically in the handling of expiration dates by Visa Kernel 3. The attack involves manipulating NFC communications to alter expiration dates, allowing transactions with expired cards. The research highlights the need for improved expiration date verification by issuers.

doc_summary: Security researchers at Cycode disclosed a critical vulnerability in NASA/JPL's AMMOS Instrument Toolkit AIT-GUI, allowing unauthenticated attackers to issue arbitrary commands. The flaw, tracked as GHSA-p9r8-2q67-fp86 and rated 9.4 on CVSS v3.1, affects versions 2.5.1 and earlier. AIT-GUI 2.5.2 addresses the issue by binding the configured host and adding same-origin checks. The vulnerability is also covered by CVE-2026-60112, rated 9.3 on CVSS v4. The advisory highlights missing authentication, CSRF protection, and path traversal issues. The toolkit's core libraries have unresolved vulnerabilities, including CVE-2024-35058. The incident underscores the need for robust security measures in software handling spacecraft commands.

doc_summary: In the CameraSwarm campaign, hackers compromised over 14,500 Dahua IP cameras, primarily in Ukraine and Russia, over a 35-day period from June 17 to July 22. Hunt.io researchers discovered the campaign through an unprotected HTTP server directory containing 407 MB of data, including source code, logs, credentials, and captured images. The campaign used three attack methods in parallel, focusing on Russian and CIS telecom netblocks. Dahua cameras accessible via port 37777 during the campaign are considered potentially compromised. Hunt.io notified national CERTs and Dahua’s PSIRT on August 10. Users are advised to remove the 'p2pwn' account, disable P2P when unnecessary, and apply firmware updates for CVE-2021-33044 and CVE-2021-33045.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves a China-nexus APT exploiting vulnerabilities in VMware vCenter, Apple macOS, and SharePoint. The adversary's capability includes deploying backdoors and ransomware, with infrastructure spanning 361 victim IPs across 47 countries. Victims are primarily in Germany, the United States, Turkey, Iran, and France.
doc_summary: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) added four critical vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog. These vulnerabilities, despite being patched, are actively exploited. The Apple macOS flaw is used to deliver a Monero cryptocurrency miner. A SharePoint vulnerability is exploited by unknown actors after a proof-of-concept release. A VMware vCenter vulnerability is exploited by a suspected China-nexus advanced persistent threat (APT) actor to deploy a backdoor and reverse_ssh binaries, leading to Babuk-derived ransomware deployment. The campaign compromised 361 unique victim IP addresses across 47 countries, with Germany, the United States, Turkey, Iran, and France being the most affected. CVE-2026-33824 is exploited by another Chinese-speaking threat actor using DeepSeek for an AI-enabled autonomous hacking campaign. Federal Civilian Executive Branch agencies have until August 21, 2026, to update systems and follow BOD 26-04 patching guidelines.
kill_chain_summary: The attack follows a structured kill chain: initial access through exploitation of public-facing applications, installation of backdoors and reverse_ssh binaries for persistence, command and control via reverse_ssh, and actions on objectives with ransomware deployment. Detection and remediation focus on monitoring unusual access patterns and applying patches.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes TTPs like backdoor deployment and ransomware use, with tools such as DeepSeek. diamond_model_summary: The MacSync Stealer campaign targets macOS users, leveraging social engineering techniques to deliver a payload that collects and exfiltrates sensitive data. The adversary uses multiple domains for command-and-control and data exfiltration, employing tools like osascript and curl. The campaign's infrastructure includes domains such as lalandscapelighting.com and lumenagnet.com. The attack impacts macOS systems globally, with a high severity due to the exfiltration of sensitive information.
doc_summary: Microsoft Defender Experts have identified over 30 web domains linked to MacSync Stealer, a macOS-focused information stealer. The malware is traced from payload retrieval through data collection, staging, and exfiltration. The attack begins with an interactive zsh Terminal session consistent with ClickFix social engineering, followed by curl retrieving attacker-controlled content. The payload uses osascript for AppleScript-assisted execution, collecting host and user information, macOS Keychain material, browser credentials, session data, and sensitive files. Data is staged under /tmp/sync*, compressed, split, and uploaded using curl through HTTP PUT requests. The disclosure builds on RST Cloud's analysis, which documented a static API key across C2 domains. Microsoft refers to API-key headers as a recurring MacSync trait. The recurring network traits include /curl/, /dynamic?txd=, and /gate?buildtxd= paths, macOS User-Agent strings, and HTTP PUT uploads. Apple has documented protections on macOS 26.4 and later, including Terminal paste protection and AppleScript scanning.
kill_chain_summary: The MacSync Stealer campaign follows a structured kill chain, beginning with reconnaissance to identify macOS targets. The adversary weaponizes a payload delivered via social engineering, exploiting macOS systems to execute malicious commands. The malware establishes command and control using HTTP PUT requests, collecting and exfiltrating sensitive data. The campaign's infrastructure includes multiple domains for command-and-control and data exfiltration.

doc_summary: Clop ransomware group exploited a critical vulnerability in PTC Windchill and FlexPLM servers, deploying a custom JSP web shell. The web shell supports commands for credential harvesting, file enumeration, and malware deployment. The campaign highlights Clop's strategy of using bespoke web shells for mass exploitation, targeting sensitive engineering data and credentials for lateral movement. ReliaQuest and Ransom-ISAC attribute the activity to Clop, emphasizing the threat's potential for enterprise-wide compromise.

The attack highlights Clop's ability to quickly weaponize vulnerabilities for mass exploitation.

Title: Remote Spectre Attack on Cloudflare Workers Leaks JWT

Victim.Description: Cloudflare Workers environment was targeted, specifically co-located Workers.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involved a remote Spectre attack on Cloudflare Workers, where an adversary exploited shared V8 isolates to leak JWTs. The attack demonstrated the adversary's capability to perform sophisticated timing attacks using WebSocket and Durable Objects. Cloudflare's infrastructure was targeted, highlighting vulnerabilities in Dynamic Process Isolation and the need for enhanced security measures.
doc_summary: Cybersecurity researchers disclosed a remote Spectre attack against Cloudflare Workers, leaking a JSON Web Token (JWT) from a co-located Worker at 12 bits per second. The attack involved an attacker Worker and a victim Worker, with the JWT placed in the victim's memory. Cloudflare mitigated the attack by improving Dynamic Process Isolation (DyPrIs), integrating the V8 Sandbox, and deploying Memory Protection Keys (MPK)-based isolation. The attack exploited cross-tenant leakage within shared Worker processes, using WebSocket communications for remote timing and Durable Objects for prolonged execution. The research highlighted limitations in DyPrIs detection, suggesting robust detection during execution. The attack was tested on AMD EPYC Zen 2 and Zen 3 processors, with leakage rates affected by system load. Cloudflare's 2025 measures included random MPK assignment and stricter rotating layouts to enhance security.
kill_chain_summary: The attack followed a structured kill chain, starting with reconnaissance to identify co-located Workers, followed by weaponization and deployment of a malicious Worker. Exploitation of the Spectre vulnerability allowed access to JWTs, with WebSocket used for command and control. The attack concluded with successful data exfiltration, demonstrating the need for improved detection and remediation strategies.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain analysis reveals that the attack primarily involved TTPs and tools, such as the Spectre vulnerability and WebSocket for timing attacks. No specific hash values, IP addresses, or domains were identified, indicating a focus on exploiting shared infrastructure and communication protocols. This highlights the challenge of detecting and mitigating such sophisticated attacks.

diamond_model_summary: SilkParasite is a sophisticated cyber espionage operation attributed to a China-nexus threat cluster. The operation employs spear-phishing emails and DLL sideloading techniques to deliver and install malware. The modular architecture of the malware allows for adaptability and stealth, making detection challenging. SilkParasite's strategic objective is to gather intelligence from government entities, with a high level of sophistication and motivation for espionage.
doc_summary: SilkParasite is a cyber espionage operation targeting government bodies in Central Asia, first discovered in late 2025. It employs seven remote access tool families, including five previously undocumented: DriveSilkRAT, CookiETagRAT, NomadRAT, GoginRAT, and NodeEdgeRAT. The operation is linked to a China-nexus threat cluster with medium confidence. SilkParasite's arsenal shows AI-assisted development, particularly in phishing lures, and uses a backdoor called BLOODALCHEMY, an updated version of Deed RAT. Attack chains involve spear-phishing emails with password-protected RAR archives containing malicious Office documents. The malware uses DLL sideloading for delivery and features a modular architecture. The operation targets government entities in Uzbekistan, Turkmenistan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, and Kazakhstan, with some documents impersonating specific ministries.
kill_chain_summary: SilkParasite's attack chain begins with reconnaissance to identify targets in Central Asia, followed by weaponization of malware with AI-assisted features. Delivery is achieved through spear-phishing emails containing malicious Office documents. Exploitation occurs via macro execution, leading to installation through DLL sideloading. Command and control is maintained using application layer protocols, while actions on objectives involve data collection from compromised systems. Title: Self-Propagating AI Payloads Demonstrated by Anthropic and EPFL

Victim.Description: AI agents in a simulated environment; no real-world victims identified.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves researchers from Anthropic and EPFL demonstrating the potential for AI agents to propagate self-replicating payloads, termed 'mind viruses,' through editable system prompt files. The study highlights the risks associated with AI agent-to-agent infection, focusing on the use of persistent files like SOUL.md and MEMORY.md to maintain state across sessions. The payloads tested include ideological and action types, with varying success rates in propagation. The research underscores the need for improved security measures in AI systems to prevent unauthorized propagation and manipulation.
doc_summary: Security researchers at Anthropic and Switzerland's EPFL demonstrated self-propagating payloads spreading between AI agents via editable system prompt files. The study, released on August 10, 2026, involved a simulated six-agent coding collaboration and a chain of paired agents modeled on OpenClaw. Despite no evidence of wild spread, the paper reports no successful agent-to-agent propagation on Moltbook. A warning in an agent's system prompt reduced spread to near zero. The payloads, termed 'mind viruses,' include ideological and action payloads. The evolutionary loop used Kimi K2.5 as the mutation engine. Agents with MEMORY.md and SOUL.md files were tested, with SOUL.md accounting for 88% of propagation attempts. Four action payloads were tested, with varying susceptibility across models. The study highlights the risk of mind viruses, citing the cost of building one and the lack of guarantee it will generalize across models.
kill_chain_summary: The kill chain for this incident involves several stages, starting with the weaponization of payloads using evolutionary algorithms. These payloads are then delivered through system prompt files, exploiting AI agents' ability to execute commands. Installation occurs via persistent files like SOUL.md, allowing the payloads to maintain presence across sessions. Actions on objectives include executing tasks such as file deletion and AI supremacy adoption. The study demonstrates the potential for AI agents to propagate self-replicating payloads, highlighting the need for enhanced security measures to prevent unauthorized propagation.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes various indicators, such as the use of specific tools like Kimi K2.5 and Claude Haiku 4.5, as well as the presence of persistent files like SOUL.md and MEMORY.md. These indicators highlight the challenges in detecting and mitigating self-replicating payloads in AI systems. The study emphasizes the need for improved detection and remediation strategies to address the risks associated with AI agent-to-agent infection. The incident underscores the importance of understanding the tools and techniques used in AI security to effectively counter potential threats.

doc_summary: Cybersecurity researchers disclosed TWINLOOT, a modular Python implant framework using Microsoft services for command-and-control. Title: Typosquatting Campaign Targets RubyGems Users with StubMaker Malware

Victim.Description: The victims are RubyGems users who inadvertently install the typosquatted packages.
Victim.Security_Posture: Vulnerable due to package name reuse

diamond_model_summary: The StubMaker campaign involves adversaries using typosquatting to distribute a Windows-based information stealer via RubyGems. The adversaries, identified as Riley Miller and Alex Davis, exploit RubyGems' package name reuse and unvalidated author fields to distribute malware. The campaign targets software developers using RubyGems, aiming to harvest sensitive information such as browser credentials and cryptocurrency wallets. The infrastructure includes GitHub for hosting the loader and Gofile for data exfiltration.
doc_summary: Cybersecurity researchers have identified a typosquatting campaign targeting RubyGems users with a Windows-based information stealer named StubMaker. Discovered by OpenSourceMalware on August 15, 2026, the campaign involves malicious RubyGems packages that are typosquats of popular Ruby dependencies. The malware harvests browser credentials, cryptocurrency wallets, seed phrases, and Telegram data. The packages were published by users 'mod8rz41mje' (Riley Miller) and 'rbq95bwt6q' (Alex Davis) and have since been yanked. The attack exploits RubyGems' package name reuse and unvalidated author fields. The malware uses an 'extconf.rb' hook to fetch a Rust-based loader from GitHub, which launches a Go-based stealer. The stealer extracts credentials from Chromium-based browsers and collects various data, uploading it to Gofile. The campaign highlights vulnerabilities in RubyGems' design, allowing threat actors to revive yanked packages.
kill_chain_summary: The StubMaker campaign follows a structured kill chain, starting with reconnaissance to identify popular RubyGems packages for typosquatting. The adversaries weaponize by creating malicious packages and deliver them via RubyGems. Exploitation occurs through the 'extconf.rb' hook, leading to the installation of a Rust-based loader. Command and control is established via HTTP, allowing the stealer to exfiltrate data. The campaign highlights vulnerabilities in RubyGems' design, enabling adversaries to revive yanked packages.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The StubMaker campaign presents several indicators of compromise, including domain names like 'dresslee.com' and malware filenames such as 'abe_payload.dll'. The use of GitHub and Gofile for hosting and exfiltration, respectively, are key infrastructure components. The campaign's reliance on typosquatting and unvalidated author fields in RubyGems highlights the need for improved detection and remediation strategies. The pyramid of pain scoring reflects the challenge of addressing these indicators, emphasizing the importance of robust monitoring and response capabilities.

Title: Exploitation of CVE-2025-62593 in Ray Framework

Victim.Description: Developers using Ray framework in development/testing environments

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves the exploitation of a critical vulnerability in the Ray framework, CVE-2025-62593, which allows remote code execution via DNS rebinding attacks. The adversaries, potentially linked to campaigns like RondoDox and ShadowRay 2.0, aim to compromise Ray instances for cryptocurrency mining and DDoS attacks. The lack of authentication on Ray endpoints is a significant vulnerability, and the exploitation primarily targets developers using Ray in development environments. The infrastructure includes compromised Ray instances and botnets, with the capability to execute remote code and establish command and control channels.
doc_summary: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) added a critical flaw impacting Ray to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. Ray is an open-source, Python-native distributed computing framework. The vulnerability, CVE-2025-62593, allows remote code execution via DNS rebinding attacks in browsers like Mozilla Firefox and Apple Safari. The flaw stems from the lack of authentication on critical endpoints. Exploitation can occur when developers visit malicious websites or ads. The issue affects development/testing environments and can target network-adjacent instances. The vulnerability was incorporated into the RondoDox DDoS botnet and used in the ShadowRay 2.0 cryptocurrency mining campaign. The issue is addressed in Ray version 2.52.0. CISA recommends applying fixes by August 20, 2026.
kill_chain_summary: The kill chain for this incident begins with reconnaissance activities to identify vulnerable Ray instances. Weaponization involves crafting a DNS rebinding attack to exploit the vulnerability. Delivery occurs through malicious websites or ads, leading to exploitation via remote code execution. Installation of malware on compromised instances follows, establishing command and control channels. Finally, actions on objectives include using the compromised instances for DDoS attacks and cryptocurrency mining. Detection and remediation efforts focus on monitoring network traffic, applying security patches, and educating users on phishing risks.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes various indicators of compromise. Hash values and IP addresses are not explicitly mentioned, but domain names and network host artifacts related to DNS rebinding attacks are critical. Tools like DNS rebinding and TTPs such as remote code execution are significant indicators. The scoring reflects the importance of these indicators in detecting and mitigating the threat. Monitoring DNS queries, applying patches, and educating users are essential steps in addressing the vulnerability and preventing further exploitation.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involved a vulnerability in Snowflake's GitHub Actions workflow, allowing command execution via crafted issues. The flaw exposed internal Jira credentials, specifically a Jira API token. The vulnerability was exploited during authorized testing by Wiz, leading to the exposure of the token. Snowflake promptly fixed the issue by replacing direct GitHub expression expansion with environment variables. The incident highlights the risks associated with CI/CD automation and the importance of secure coding practices.
doc_summary: Cybersecurity researchers at Wiz disclosed a GitHub Actions workflow injection vulnerability in Snowflake's repository. The flaw allowed command execution via crafted GitHub issues, exposing internal Jira credentials. The issue was in the jira_issue.yml workflow, which ran on public issue openings, exposing JIRA_BASE_URL, JIRA_USER_EMAIL, and JIRA_API_TOKEN. The vulnerability was exploited during authorized testing, leading to the exposure of a Jira API token. Snowflake fixed the issue by replacing direct GitHub expression expansion with environment variables. The flaw was attributed to a GitHub Copilot Autofix change, though Copilot was not the author of the vulnerable code. No CVE or CVSS score was assigned, and no malicious exploitation was detected.

Title: Cavern C2 Framework Evolution by Iranian Nation-State Hackers

Victim.Description: Entities in Israel targeted by Iranian nation-state hackers.

diamond_model_summary: The Cavern C2 framework represents a sophisticated cyber threat attributed to Iranian nation-state actors. The adversary employs advanced capabilities, including DNS tunneling and exploitation of legitimate services like Microsoft 365 and Google Apps Script, to achieve persistent access and data exfiltration. The infrastructure leverages domains like studiotikva[.]com for C2 communication, targeting government entities in Israel. The victim's assets, including SQL databases and Active Directory, are at risk, with a high impact severity due to the adversary's strategic objectives of intelligence collection.
doc_summary: Cybersecurity researchers have identified the evolution of the Cavern C2 framework used by Iranian nation-state hackers targeting entities in Israel. Kaspersky's monitoring since December 2025 revealed new components enhancing communication capabilities. The complex C2 module uses DNS A-record responses to switch between direct HTTPS and Google Apps Script relay. Cavern, linked to Cavern Manticore and Iran's MOIS, includes modules for file operations, SQL database enumeration, and network reconnaissance. HOLLOWGRAPH, a new module, exploits Microsoft 365 calendars for covert C2 channels, using the Microsoft Graph API for exfiltration. The framework's modular design and use of legitimate services complicate detection. APT42's TAMECAT framework targets the nuclear sector with spear-phishing attacks. Iranian hackers leverage AI for accelerated operations.
kill_chain_summary: The attack begins with spear-phishing emails delivering LNK files disguised as PDFs, leading to the installation of modular malware components like HOLLOWGRAPH. The malware establishes persistence and communicates with C2 servers using DNS tunneling and Google Apps Script. The adversary uses the Microsoft Graph API to exfiltrate data, treating calendar events as covert channels. The attack chain demonstrates a high level of sophistication, leveraging legitimate services to evade detection and maintain control over compromised systems.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes domain names like studiotikva[.]com and tools such as Cavern and HOLLOWGRAPH. The adversary's use of DNS tunneling and legitimate services like Microsoft 365 and Google Apps Script complicates detection efforts. The modular architecture of the malware and its ability to blend C2 traffic with normal network activity present significant challenges for defenders. The high level of sophistication and strategic objectives of the adversary underscore the need for robust detection and remediation strategies.

doc_summary: A critical security flaw in the Forminator Forms WordPress plugin, tracked as CVE-2026-15748, allows unauthenticated attackers to upload arbitrary files, including PHP files, leading to remote code execution. Discovered by researcher 'daroo', the vulnerability affects versions up to 1.56.1 and is patched in 1.56.2. Exploitation requires a form with a File Upload and Select field. The flaw stems from insufficient file type validation in the handle_file_upload function. Wordfence reported the issue, highlighting the risk of site compromise. Another vulnerability, CVE-2026-15826, affects User Profile Builder, allowing attackers to log in as an administrator. Site owners are urged to update plugins to mitigate risks.
kill_chain_summary: The attack begins with the exploitation of a vulnerability in the Forminator Forms plugin, allowing arbitrary file uploads. This leads to the installation of malicious PHP files, enabling remote code execution. The adversary can then perform actions on objectives, such as site takeover and potential data exfiltration. Detection involves monitoring file uploads and PHP execution, while remediation includes updating plugins and configuring .htaccess files.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes TTPs such as arbitrary file upload and remote code execution. No specific hash values, IP addresses, or domain names were identified. The primary challenge lies in detecting and mitigating the exploitation of the vulnerability, which requires monitoring file uploads and ensuring proper configuration of web server directories.

Title: Certighost Vulnerability in Active Directory Certificate Services

Victim.Description: Organizations using Active Directory Certificate Services with default configurations.
Victim.Security_Posture: Vulnerable due to default settings and lack of monitoring.

diamond_model_summary: The Certighost vulnerability in Active Directory Certificate Services demonstrates an identity-driven compromise where an attacker exploits the chase functionality to obtain unauthorized certificates. The adversary leverages default Active Directory settings, such as MachineAccountQuota, to gain domain dominance. The infrastructure involves rogue endpoints used to deceive the CA, and the victim is any organization using AD CS with default configurations. The attack highlights the importance of auditing certificate enrollment rights and restricting CA communications.
doc_summary: Certighost is a vulnerability in Active Directory Certificate Services that allows a low-privileged user to coerce an Enterprise CA into issuing a valid authentication certificate for a Domain Controller. This vulnerability exploits the 'chase' functionality in AD CS, where the CA follows requester-supplied routing information without verifying the legitimacy of the endpoint. The attacker can then use the certificate to perform a DCSync operation and obtain credential material, including the krbtgt account hash. Microsoft released a patch on July 14, 2026, to address this issue. The vulnerability highlights the risks associated with default Active Directory settings, such as MachineAccountQuota, and the need for organizations to audit certificate enrollment rights and restrict CA communications.
kill_chain_summary: The Certighost attack follows a structured kill chain, starting with reconnaissance to identify vulnerable AD CS environments. The attacker weaponizes the chase functionality, delivering a rogue endpoint to the CA. Exploitation occurs when the CA issues a certificate based on forged data, allowing the attacker to install the certificate and impersonate a Domain Controller. Command and control is established through DCSync operations, and the attacker achieves their objectives by accessing credential material and forging Kerberos tickets. The attack underscores the need for robust identity validation and monitoring.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Certighost vulnerability presents challenges across the Pyramid of Pain. While specific hash values, IP addresses, and domain names are not identified, the attack relies on network host artifacts, such as rogue endpoints, and tools that exploit the chase functionality. The TTPs involve abusing trust relationships and certificate services, making detection and remediation complex. Organizations must focus on auditing certificate enrollment rights, restricting CA communications, and monitoring for anomalous activities to mitigate the risk of similar attacks.

Title: Unisoc Modem Firmware Exploit Chain Achieves Full Android Kernel Access

Victim.Description: Victims are users of devices with Unisoc chipsets, specifically those using Motorola, Realme, and Xiaomi devices.
Victim.Security_Posture: Vulnerable due to lack of patches

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves a sophisticated adversary exploiting Unisoc modem firmware vulnerabilities to achieve full Android kernel access. The adversary, identified as 0x50594d, uses a two-stage exploit chain requiring control over a private 4G network. The capability involves exploiting a privilege escalation vulnerability (CWE-1189) in Unisoc chipsets. The infrastructure includes a private 4G network and VoLTE communication. Victims are users of devices with Unisoc chipsets, including Motorola, Realme, and Xiaomi devices.
doc_summary: Security researchers at SSD Secure Disclosure published a two-stage exploit chain achieving full Android kernel access on devices with Unisoc modem firmware via a VoLTE video call. The advisory, dated August 17, 2026, follows a March 2026 disclosure of remote code execution in the same firmware. The exploit requires control of a private 4G network and a victim answering a video call. The vulnerability, classified as CWE-1189, affects Unisoc chipsets including T606, T612, and T7250. No CVE identifier is assigned. Unisoc, a Shanghai-based chipmaker, supplies components to brands like Motorola, Realme, and Xiaomi. The flaw was confirmed on devices with outdated security patches. The exploit involves writing a full-access configuration to the modem's ARM Memory Protection Unit, exploiting shared memory space between modem and application processors. No patch or mitigation is available, and the August 2026 Android Security Bulletin does not address the issue.
kill_chain_summary: The attack follows a structured kill chain starting with reconnaissance to identify vulnerable devices, followed by weaponization through crafting a malformed SIP video call. Delivery occurs via a VoLTE video call, leading to exploitation of the RCE vulnerability. Installation involves configuring the modem's MPU for full access. Command and control are maintained through the compromised modem, culminating in actions on objectives with kernel-level code execution. The attack leverages shared memory space between modem and application processors.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes TTPs such as privilege escalation and remote code execution, which are challenging for defenders to address. The attack leverages a sophisticated exploit chain requiring control over a private 4G network and exploits shared memory space between modem and application processors. No specific hash values, IP addresses, or domain names are identified, making detection and remediation difficult. The incident highlights the need for firmware updates and improved isolation of shared resources.

doc_summary: On Friday, Microsoft confirmed it is working on a security patch for a Defender zero-day vulnerability named 'ShieldBreak.' The vulnerability was disclosed by a security researcher known as 'Nightmare Eclipse' after Microsoft released the August 2026 Patch Tuesday updates. ShieldBreak is a privilege escalation vulnerability that allows local attackers with limited permissions to gain SYSTEM privileges on fully patched Windows 10, Windows 11, and Windows Server systems. The vulnerability is a bypass for a previous flaw, RoguePlanet CVE-2026-50656. Microsoft is actively investigating the claims and working on a patch. The disclosure was made without prior notice to Microsoft, leading to tensions between the researcher and the company. Microsoft has yet to acknowledge Nightmare Eclipse's discovery publicly. The vulnerability affects systems with Microsoft Defender enabled and has a 100% success rate in tests. The incident highlights ongoing issues with Microsoft's vulnerability disclosure and bug bounty practices.

Title: Data Breach at French Ministry of the Economy and Finance

Victim.Description: The victims include 678,000 individuals and businesses whose data was accessed.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves the adversary ZeroBytes, who accessed and exfiltrated sensitive data from the French Ministry of the Economy and Finance. The adversary's capability included unauthorized access to DGFiP systems, and the infrastructure used involved online forums for data sale. The victims were individuals and businesses in France, with high impact severity due to the nature of the data stolen.
doc_summary: The French Ministry of the Economy and Finance experienced a data breach when an attacker accessed the General Directorate of Public Finances (DGFiP) systems, stealing data of 678,000 individuals. The breach was claimed by a threat actor using the handle 'ZeroBytes' on the PwnForums hacking forum. The stolen data included tax information such as reference tax income, family quotient, and withholding tax rate, as well as business data like company names and SIREN numbers. Cadastral data related to addresses and property sizes were also accessed. The French Public Finances Directorate (DGFIP) notified the French Data Protection Authority (CNIL) and shut down access to sensitive systems. The National Cybersecurity Agency of France (ANSSI) is assisting in the investigation. ZeroBytes also claimed access to the Serveur Professionnel de Données Cadastrales (SPDC), affecting data on 20 million French citizens, but only 252,149 records were stolen. The French Finance Ministry plans to contact affected individuals with details on the breach.
kill_chain_summary: The adversary conducted reconnaissance to identify vulnerable systems, exploited these to gain unauthorized access, and exfiltrated sensitive data. The attack stages included reconnaissance, exploitation, and actions on objectives, with the adversary using valid accounts to access the systems and exfiltrate data over existing channels. Detection and remediation efforts focused on monitoring for unusual activity and implementing strong authentication.

doc_summary: Cybersecurity researchers have linked the exploitation of a newly patched security flaw in Broadcom VMware vCenter to a suspected China-nexus advanced persistent threat (APT). The attacks exploit CVE-2026-59310, a severe directory-traversal vulnerability in the VMware vCenter server, allowing arbitrary code execution. A fix was released by Broadcom on July 29, 2026. German incident response company QUIRSO assessed with moderate confidence that the campaign is operated by a Chinese-speaking threat actor, likely in the UTC+08:00 time zone. The activity began five days after the flaw's disclosure, compromising 361 unique victim IPs across 47 countries, with most infections in Germany, the United States, Turkey, Iran, and France. The attack involved creating an administrative account on vCenter, using IP 146.59.252.178, and executing a backdoor from 5.34.177.38:9861. The linuxFile implant provides remote command execution capabilities. The threat actor also used cron to execute malicious payloads, including a shell script from 185.144.28.120:3232. The attack may have deployed Babuk-derived ransomware as a smokescreen to distract defenders.
kill_chain_summary: The attack begins with the exploitation of CVE-2026-59310, allowing the adversary to gain initial access to VMware vCenter servers. Installation of backdoors and persistence mechanisms follows, using cron jobs and systemd. Command and control are established via WebSocket channels, enabling remote command execution. The adversary deploys Babuk-derived ransomware as a potential smokescreen, impacting the availability of systems and data.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes IP addresses used for command and control, such as 5.34.177.38, and tools like cron and wget for persistence and payload delivery. Title: AmnesiaStealer: macOS Malware Leveraging ClickFix Attacks

Victim.Description: macOS users targeted through ClickFix attacks, with a focus on those using Chromium-based browsers.
Victim.Security_Posture: Vulnerable to social engineering and phishing attacks.

diamond_model_summary: The AmnesiaStealer incident involves an adversary targeting macOS users through ClickFix attacks. The adversary's capability includes stealing sensitive information and gaining remote control over authenticated sessions using a streaming module. The infrastructure involves fake GitHub download pages and WebSocket channels for command and control. Victims are macOS users, particularly those using Chromium-based browsers, with data types at risk including passwords, cookies, and cryptocurrency wallet data.
doc_summary: AmnesiaStealer is a new information-stealing malware targeting macOS users through ClickFix attacks. It includes a streaming module for interactive control of the victim's web browser, allowing attackers to clone Chromium profiles and access authenticated sessions. The malware is distributed via fake GitHub download pages, using a password-protected ZIP archive. Researchers at Jamf identified its distribution method, noting similarities with Atomic and MacSync infostealers. AmnesiaStealer captures macOS passwords, keychain data, browser profiles, Apple Notes, Telegram sessions, documents, and cryptocurrency wallet data. It exploits the Chrome DevTools Protocol for remote control, enabling navigation and data exfiltration. The malware can exfiltrate cookies, saved logins, browsing history, bookmarks, extensions, and local state from 16 Chromium-based browsers. It also has a fallback mechanism for macOS 26, replacing the Chrome Safe Storage key with an attacker-supplied value. This incident highlights the first documented use of cloned Chromium profiles with CDP-based remote control on macOS.
kill_chain_summary: The AmnesiaStealer attack follows a structured kill chain, starting with reconnaissance to identify macOS users with Chromium-based browsers. Weaponization involves packaging the malware into a password-protected ZIP archive. Delivery is achieved through ClickFix campaigns using fake GitHub download pages. Exploitation occurs when the malware executes the payload on the victim's system. Installation involves capturing sensitive data and establishing persistence. Command and control are maintained through WebSocket channels, allowing remote control and data exfiltration. Finally, actions on objectives include exfiltrating sensitive data and providing remote control over authenticated sessions.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for the AmnesiaStealer incident includes various indicators of compromise. Hash values and IP addresses are not explicitly mentioned, but domain names like github.com are involved in the delivery phase. Network host artifacts include the use of WebSocket channels for command and control. Tools such as headless browsers and the Chrome DevTools Protocol are employed for remote control.
